android/performance/startup.md: You tap the app icon. A spinner appears, then you wait for the feed. The app has shown something, but it has not yet delivered what you came for. Optimising that launch starts with choosing which finish line matters.
android/performance/jank.md: A feed scroll catches even though no network request is running. The missing evidence is one frame: did app code run too long, wait for another thread, or finish while rendering downstream fell behind?
android/performance/rendering.md: A trace shows the main thread finishing its work, yet the frame still appears late. Drawing commands are only one handoff. Something must execute them, provide the buffer, and present it on the display.
android/performance/anrs.md: The Save button stops responding. Main is waiting on a lock, but the lock’s owner is waiting for disk. Moving the button handler alone would miss the chain that made the interaction unresponsive.
android/performance/memory-management-an: Open a profile, go back, repeat. The old screens should be irrelevant, yet a listener registry still points to each one. Memory growth is now an ownership problem: who promised to remove those references?
android/performance/native-memory-bitmap: The image feed disappears on a small device, while the Kotlin heap chart looks ordinary. Pixel storage, native allocations and graphics buffers also consume memory. One heap chart cannot account for the whole process.
android/performance/app-size-and-r8.md: A feature works in development and fails only in the shipped build. At the same time its SDK adds download weight. The release artifact must answer two questions: what code survived, and what did the user actually download?
android/performance/baseline-profiles.md: A newly installed app feels slower on its first useful journey than after repeated use. If runtime compilation contributes to that difference, a profile can tell ART which paths deserve preparation. It still needs to match the shipped code.
android/performance/macrobenchmark-and-p: A pull request turns the startup benchmark red. Before changing code, check that it still loads the same content on the same device and compilation state. A faster empty screen is not a successful experiment.
android/performance/battery-power-profil: The app is idle on screen, yet the battery chart keeps moving. A retry loop, location session or wake lock may be keeping hardware busy. Start by identifying the work that continues after useful activity ends.
android/performance/network-radio-wakeup: Read receipts arrive one by one, each triggering a tiny request. The bytes look small, but the app keeps asking the network to work. A freshness requirement is needed before deciding what can wait for a batch.
android/performance/thermal-low-end-devi: The demo is smooth for a minute, then video previews compete with scrolling as the device warms. A fixed “high quality” setting cannot express the smaller work budget available later in the session.
android/observability/logging.md: A release logger ignores a debug message, but the expensive expression inside that message still runs. Logging has two boundaries: constructing the argument and deciding what reaches a sink.
android/observability/crash-monitoring.m: A rollout adds a new crash cluster. The stack is partly minified, the affected users share a device cohort, and the report arrives after the failure. Useful monitoring must connect this evidence to the exact build and an owner.
android/observability/mobile-apm-and-rum: The backend reports a quick response, but the user waits for checkout to update. The two clocks may measure different work. Start by naming the client interaction boundary before comparing dashboards.
